candidate_sentence_map.S1: VILVI Group reported strong revenue growth but significantly lower operating profitability in the first quarter of 2026.
candidate_sentence_map.S2: Consolidated revenue increased 22.4% year on year to EUR 86.97 million, supported by higher sales in Lithuania and other countries and the consolidation of Marijampolės pieno konservai UAB from 1 January 2026.
candidate_sentence_map.S3: Revenue from Lithuania rose 72.9% to EUR 14.63 million, while revenue from other countries increased 46.6% to EUR 29.82 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S4: European Union revenue was broadly stable at EUR 42.52 million, representing 49% of total sales compared with 59% a year earlier.
candidate_sentence_map.S6: Cheese, cheese products and other sales declined 28.8% to EUR 37.64 million, representing 43% of revenue compared with 75% in Q1 2025.
candidate_sentence_map.S7: Dry milk product revenue more than doubled, rising 126.9% to EUR 24.66 million, while fresh milk product revenue increased 73.4% to EUR 12.75 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S8: Canned milk products contributed EUR 11.92 million following the acquisition of Marijampolės pieno konservai.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: EBITDA fell 50.2% to EUR 3.00 million, and the EBITDA margin decreased from 8.5% to 3.5%.
candidate_sentence_map.S10: The report states that Q1 2026 EBITDA excludes EUR 5.5 million of preliminary negative goodwill related to the Marijampolės pieno konservai acquisition.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: Despite the lower EBITDA, net profit increased 25.7% to EUR 5.09 million, compared with EUR 4.05 million in the prior-year period, and earnings per share rose from EUR 0.34 to EUR 0.43.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: Operating profit increased to EUR 6.00 million from EUR 4.72 million, reflecting EUR 5.66 million of other operating income, compared with EUR 0.08 million in Q1 2025.
candidate_sentence_map.S13: Higher finance costs, which increased to EUR 0.87 million from EUR 0.45 million, partly offset this improvement.
candidate_sentence_map.S15: The Group completed the acquisition of 100% of Marijampolės pieno konservai on 16 January 2026 and began commercial cheese production at its new Baltic Dairy Board factory in Bauska, Latvia.
candidate_sentence_map.S16: The facility is expected to create more than 100 jobs, produce up to 18,000 tons of cheese annually and export to more than 40 countries.
candidate_sentence_map.S17: Net financial debt increased 89.7% to EUR 83.43 million, while total assets rose to EUR 220.31 million from EUR 188.98 million at year-end 2025.
candidate_sentence_map.S18: Operating cash flow remained negative at EUR 9.63 million, although it improved from negative EUR 12.80 million in Q1 2025.
candidate_sentence_map.S19: Cash at the end of March was EUR 0.95 million.

evaluation.label: Generally yes

issues.description: While S6, S7, and S8 provide detailed breakdowns of revenue changes by product category, there is no explicit explanation of how these changes relate to the overall revenue growth mentioned in S1 and S2. The summary does not clarify whether the growth in some categories (e.g., dry milk, fresh milk, canned milk) fully offsets the decline in others (cheese, cheese products) to achieve the reported 22.4% overall revenue increase.

evaluation.justification: The candidate summary is generally coherent with no severe contradictions. The structure follows a logical flow from revenue to profitability, acquisitions, and balance sheet items. However, there is a notable logical gap in the explanation of revenue composition changes (S6, S7, S8) relative to the overall revenue growth stated in S1 and S2. While the summary provides percentages for each product category, it does not explicitly reconcile how these changes combine to produce the 22.4% overall revenue increase. This creates a minor gap in the logical chain. There are no self-contradictions, organizational issues, or unnecessary repetition. Arithmetic differences (e.g., segment vs. consolidated figures) are not contradictions because the candidate does not claim exhaustive additivity.
